title: Too slow: a stronger formulation and a rolling horizon

questions.heading: The Aggregated Outage Row Lets the LP Buy a Fraction of an Outage
questions.stem: A substation has 10 candidates and the LP relaxation replaces one of them in year t. Under the aggregated outage row, how much of that year's outage variable must the LP pay for?

options.text: All of it, since o keeps its 0-1 values in the relaxation
options.says: The page: the LP is satisfied by o = 0.1, one tenth of an outage.

options.text: None of it, since 10 o may stay at 0 with 1 unit replaced
options.says: The page: o = 0.1 and nothing less satisfies the row; the LP pays $30k.

options.text: Half of it, since the row splits the 10 units' outage in two
options.says: The page: one tenth of an outage, at one tenth of its $300k.

options.text: A tenth of it, since 10 times o must cover just 1 unit
options.says: Right: the LP buys a fraction of the outage; per-unit rows force o to 1.

questions.heading: The Design Decision: Strengthen the Formulation First, Then Decompose If Still Needed
questions.stem: Why does the project change the outage rows before it relies on the rolling horizon?

options.text: It changes no plan, only how cheaply a plan can be proved good
options.says: Right: same 0-1 plans, a tighter bound.

options.text: It is quicker to build, since the per-unit form has fewer rows
options.says: The per-unit form has about three times the rows.

options.text: It gives up the proof, but finds good plans more quickly
options.says: It keeps the proof; it is the rolling horizon that has none.

options.text: It needs no new tests, since the 0-1 plans are the same
options.says: The step adds a test that the bound drops and the optimum stays.

questions.heading: The Tests Pin the Bound, the Same Optimum, and the Rolling Plan's Rules
questions.stem: A rolling-horizon plan comes back from the last window with status OPTIMAL. Why does the project still run `violations` on it?

options.text: The status is OPTIMAL in every window, so it proves the whole plan
options.says: The bound returned is only the last window's; nothing proves the whole plan.

options.text: `violations` computes the bound the rolling horizon cannot give
options.says: It checks rules, line by line; the bound comes from a full solve.

options.text: No solve proves the whole plan, so code apart from the model checks it
options.says: Right: plain Python recomputes every rule from the plan.

options.text: Its bound is the full model's, so only the rules remain to check
options.says: Its bound is only the last window's.
